_note: Reputation (game-design §7.1-7.4, docs/diplomacy-design.md §3.1, war-and-realm §2.2). Two reputations per faction on the same axes, each -100..100: the ruler's (moves fast, weighs more) and the House's (the dynasty's slow memory). A deed moves the ruler's axis by its value and the House's by house_rate of it; during the first-impressions window (first_impressions turns after a new ruler) both move first_impressions_factor times faster. Labels show past +-label_at with tooltips listing the deeds. Perceived reputation blends ruler and House by distance: weight near_weight on the ruler for neighbours (capitals within near_metres) falling to far_weight beyond far_metres. Standing (war-and-realm §2.2): love = the mean of the kind axes' positive values, fear = the mean of the harsh axes' strength; Loved when love >= standing_at and above fear, Feared when fear >= standing_at, else Neutral; powerful when the faction's strength is at least powerful_share x the strongest faction's or among the top powerful_rank. House reputations are seeded at campaign start from the faction's tendencies (seed); afterwards the world judges deeds. Decrees and suspicion attach later (hooks). PLACEHOLDER numbers.
